reviews.title: The Maze Runner
reviews.review: Really interesting conceptually, but the first 30 minutes are the best part of the movie. I found myself looking down at my phone a lot to realize how little time has passed since I started the movie. The twist at the end was also not set up or foreshadowed in the slightest, which leaves a bad taste in my mouth.

reviews.title: Spider-Man: Brand New Day
reviews.review: After watching every other live action Spider-Man movie in the past 24-hours, I can confidently say that this is my favorite one. Tom Holland has always been my favorite Spider-Man, his movies have always had a certain vibe, but the tonal shift in this movie is insane. It manages to keep the comedy, but adds incredible action on-par with the TASM movies (Andrew) and emotional storytelling reminiscent of the 2000s trilogy (Tobey). This was Tom's best performances as Peter and Spider-Man, I shed a tear at the emotional scenes. This movie really feels like a blend of every single Spider-Man…

reviews.title: Spider-Man: No Way Home
reviews.review: Man, the end of this movie still hits like a truck; I teared up multiple times in those final scenes. Seeing the full stories of both Andrew and Tobey's Spider-Man before this made their inclusion in this movie all the more satisfying. A beautiful end for them, and a new beginning for Tom's Spider-Man. I couldn't be more excited for Brand New Day.

reviews.title: Spider-Man: Far From Home
reviews.review: This movie gets way too much hate for what it is. I agree that Spider-Man seems off when he's in Prague, London, or Berlin, but that doesn't take away from the quality of the movie itself to me. The action is a real standout here, I loved every scene and how they really focused on Peter's spidey-sense. The comedy, while still great, was a step down from Homecoming, though, certain jokes definitely fell flat for me. The writing was a lot less tight, too; many events didn't properly lead into the other and there were some pretty useless side plots taking up time near the end.

reviews.title: Spider-Man: Homecoming
reviews.review: Spider-Main: Homecoming is the Spider-Man movie I grew up with. This was the one my childhood self looked to for motivation, and I'm so glad it was. Tom Holland's Spider-Man is nothing like Tobey's or Andrew's, and their worlds couldn't be any more different. Somehow though, Tom continues to embody the same ideas of perseverance and resilience. A couple scenes near the climax really rocked me to my core, that’s what makes this movie stand out.

reviews.title: The Amazing Spider-Man 2
reviews.review: I came into this movie expecting a much worse movie than the first, but I’m glad to say I was pleasantly surprised. Hans Zimmer’s score works amazingly for this movie and it has the best action and web swinging out of any Spider-Man movie I’ve seen. Again though, like TASM 1, the ideas really work and it’s truly interesting the direction the writers went with things, but they can’t manage to stick the landing. The ending is all over the place and the villains fall flat near the end. It’s sad how Andrew Garfield was treated, he was an incredible actor for Peter and Spider-Man. He deserved a…

reviews.title: The Amazing Spider-Man
reviews.review: This is a really hard movie to rate. On one hand, I really appreciate a lot of the conceptual and technical things in this movie. Changing Peter's personality from before the bite, focusing on Gwen, and the Lizard as a main villain are all very interesting choices, but the writing struggles to bring them together well. Peter and Gwen's chemistry together is off the charts, their romance is the best part of the whole movie, but the other aspects don't reach those same heights. I love the action and the swinging, though, the 5-year gap from Spider-Man 3 to this movie is clear in…

reviews.title: Spider-Man 3
reviews.review: Everything that Spider-Man 2 did right as a sequel, Spider-Man 3 does wrong. It manages to completely unravel plot threads that have lasted the past two movies, and even its new villains are given little to no proper motivations on why they are after Spider-Man. Also, the pattern of "oh no! MJ's been kidnapped by the villain" gets old after three movies of it happening in a row. Still, the action is great and there are some genuinely good moments, mostly when Peter had the symbiote, so I can't dock it too many points.

reviews.title: Spider-Man 2
reviews.review: Spider-Man 2 juggles both continued plot threads from the first movie as well as entirely new challenges for Spider-Man to face incredibly to create one of the quintessential comic-book-movie sequels. The acting was a mixed bag; Molina's performance as Dr. Octavius works to create yet another extremely threatening villain, but I wasn't as convinced by Tobey Maguire's. The visuals are a clear step up from the previous installment, it is clear much more time and effort was put into them. Overall, an excellent watch and I sure hope the third movie continues the trend of getting…

reviews.title: Spider-Man
reviews.review: I'm clearly not as high on this movie as a lot of other people, but that doesn't take away from how influential and well-made this movie is, especially for its time. The action and performances were a standout for me, especially Willem Dafoe's as Norman Osborne. I love how the perception that New York has of Spider-Man is a real influence on the plot, it makes the entire world feel more lived in. Some of the story, however, feels off sometimes; the pacing of the beginning was much slowed than the end, and Green Goblin's motivations are never fully made clear. Nonetheless a…

reviews.title: Mercy
reviews.review: Complete slop. Reminds me of War of the Worlds, which is not a good sign at all. Somehow managed to create dozens of new plot lines by the third act resolve none of them.

reviews.title: Other Side of the Box
reviews.review: This short film builds suspense and creepiness very well, but is held back by its acting and ending.

reviews.title: Eyes Wide Shut
reviews.review: Eyes Wide Shut made me think, and it’ll take much more than just its runtime to dissect every little thing Kubrick meant to convey. I really appreciated Tom Cruise’s performance, its the best I’ve seen from him (likely because I’ve otherwise only ever seen him in the Mission: Impossible movies). I’d love to rewatch this movie, it seems like something that would reveal a lot more on a second viewing.

reviews.title: The Odyssey
reviews.review: The Odyssey is 2 hours and 53 minutes of pure filmmaking genius on display by one of the greatest directors still active today. It's a film so impactful that very little can encompass all that it is, but I can try.This film encompasses all that makes Christopher Nolan's filmography so great. The scale hits as hard as Inception, the performances resonate with me to the level of those in Oppenheimer, and the raw emotions I felt are equal to those in Interstellar.In regards to the scale, the use of music contributes just as much as anything with the camera. Ludwig Göransson's…

reviews.title: Sleepy Hollow
reviews.review: Tim Burton’s style is so clear throughout the entire runtime… the colors and cinematography are unlike any other director. This is such a classic story, full of tropes and traditions iconic to the time the original story was written. By now some of those things are cliche, however, so the story is a little held back.

reviews.title: The Cabin in the Woods
reviews.review: One of the most insane and outlandish pieces of media I’ve consumed in quite a while. It’s so cliche that it manages to be completely unpredictable…

reviews.title: Obsession
reviews.review: I know I’m a little late to the party but let me say, I’m so glad I finally watched this movie. Obsession is one of the few movies that I’d say I have absolutely no notes on, in the sense of how it is written. The script was extremely tight, every plot thread was executed so well it truly is an impressive feat. I came out the movie extremely unsettled, but also equally as impressed. Inde Navarrette’s performance deserves just as much praise. She manages to be so expressive and clearly demonstrate the magic of the One Wish Willow purely with her mannerisms.

reviews.title: Swapped
reviews.review: It’s been a while since I’ve watched a movie that was clearly aimed towards kids, so I expected your average modern Disney movie (i.e. a not very good movie). However, I was pleasantly surprised with the amount of real lessons and heart that was put into Swapped. At its core the movie is about learning what it’s like to be in someone else’s shoes, quite literally, and that message is taught alongside a story that isn’t without its plot twists. A full package of a beautiful art style and good voice acting performances pushes this movie to really be enjoyable.

reviews.title: Click
reviews.review: I came expecting a dumb Adam Sandler film, and that’s exactly what I got. However, there were some good messages about work-life balance sprinkled into the madness so I gotta give it some credit.

reviews.title: Ex Machina
reviews.review: Ex Machina is beautifully shot, with equally as beautiful of a score to go along with it. It feels like a movie that I could sit and think about for a long time even after finishing it. It’s message isn’t as clear-cut as other movies that tell the same story about power dynamics in relationships, but I’d say that makes it more powerful; you have to find the message rather than be presented with it.

reviews.title: Gone Girl
reviews.review: This might have been the biggest turnaround I’ve had on my opinion of a movie from beginning to end I’ve ever had. The start seemed to be riddled with issues and plot holes and outright chaos, but every loose end is (mostly) tied up and the ending is truly satisfying. I love how there isn’t a single likable character in the whole thing, it’s just one bad decision and horrible person after another.

reviews.title: Toy Story 5
reviews.review: A very very timely sequel that deals with a real issue with kids nowadays… and it handles that idea perfectly. I could see more from the Toy Story franchise.

reviews.title: Passengers
reviews.review: I have.. mixed feelings about this movie. First, the good: the acting is quite good for most of the runtime from both Jennifer Lawrence and Chris Pratt. Also, the premise is a really really good idea that ties in heavy themes of consent, romance, and betrayal. However, everything seems to be cast off for a typical action-packed ending sequence in the last thirty minutes, leaving me dissapointed. This movie had potential to be great, it really did, but it falls flat in too many areas for me to give it a high rating.

reviews.title: Michael
reviews.review: I mean… it’s Michael Jackson, of course the movie is peak. The set design and the use of CGI was done so well to really make it seem like everything was filmed in the ‘70s and ‘80s. And, of course, the music and sound design was incredible.

reviews.title: The Lord of the Rings: The Fellowship of the Ring
reviews.review: Believe it or not, this is my first time watching this movie… I’m planning on watching all three extended cut editions with my dad while we build the Eye of Sauron LEGO set. I don’t think the timings are going to match up, though, we’ve finished more than half of the set and we only finished one movie. It’s a whopping 3 hours 50 minutes long… but I wasn’t bored or tired of it for a second. I’ve read the books, and the extra length the movie has really allows it to flesh out the world and characters that Tolkien masterfully created. It’s amazing that the visuals of this movie still hold up…

reviews.title: Disclosure Day
reviews.review: This Steven Spielberg guy is pretty good at directing movies… if he keeps this up he could really go places.

reviews.title: F1
reviews.review: To be honest, as I was rewatching the movie I was thinking of lowering the previous score I gave it for this time, but man do those racing scenes just pull me in. It’s pretty obvious the guy who directed this also directed Top Gun: Maverick. The action is just as good.

reviews.title: Lost in Starlight
reviews.review: This movie was so so incredible, I couldn’t recommend it more. The voice acting, the animation, the directing, all outstanding. Initially, it seems like a very cliche plot, but all my expectations were subverted in the second half.

reviews.title: Legally Blonde
reviews.review: I’m surprised I hadn’t seen this earlier, I understand why it’s a classic. It’s a really optimistic film with a great message to send.

reviews.title: Backrooms
reviews.review: yoOO this movie is one of the most unsettling horror movies I’ve seen… I’m so glad Kane Parsons directed this, because it really emulates the feeling of watching YouTube series perfectly (especially with the found footage scenes). Having played the Backrooms games, I got reminded of why those games are so terrifying… I can’t wait for the sequel.

reviews.title: The Devil Wears Prada
reviews.review: This movie dealt with some interesting themes and dynamics… I especially liked the interactions between Anne Hathaway and Stanley Tucci’s characters. Now I have to watch the sequel 🤔.

reviews.title: Pretty Woman
reviews.review: This plot of this movie is exactly what I think of when I think of a romance movie… it’s really got all the ups and downs you’d expect. Nonetheless, an enjoyable movie to watch 👍.

reviews.title: Nope
reviews.review: With both this movie and Get Out, Jordan Peele continues to show me how incredible he is at writing horror. Some of those scenes really made my heart pound more than I’m willing to admit. Nope also gives a completely unique perspective to the alien/sci-fi genre, subverting my expectations on many instances. At the same time, it manages to have real emotional moments that hit hard. Now I have to watch Us to see if all of his horror movies are this good…

reviews.title: The Drama
reviews.review: This movie wasn’t what I thought it would be… it had some really interesting elements that came together quite well at the end. The third act is what made the movie truly great for me, the performances by both Zendaya and Pattinson were incredible. Surprisingly funny too.

reviews.title: The Sheep Detectives
reviews.review: A charming, wholesome, and hilarious story about a flock of sheep who really love their shepherd :). The movie deals with themes of grief and inclusion, which makes it a really good movie for kids, but it also manages to hook in older audiences too with just how well it’s written. The voice performances were all very well done, too.

reviews.title: Spider-Man: No Way Home
reviews.review: First rewatch since I first watched it in 2021.. and this movie is incredible. I’m not afraid to admit I teared up at the ending, I can’t wait to see its repercussions in Spider-Man: Brand New Day.

reviews.title: Incantation
reviews.review: scary 😨 very very spooky scary 😨

reviews.title: Lucy
reviews.review: this is the MOST fever dream movie I’ve ever watched another side of the 2 am movie spectrum…

reviews.title: Slumdog Millionaire
reviews.review: perfect movie to watch at 2 am 😢 somehow manages to balance incredible editing and cinematography to make suspenseful and sad moments truly come to life.. an incredible movie through and through

reviews.title: The Super Mario Galaxy Movie
reviews.review: A very fun movie with really colorful and fluid animation. I do wish it was longer, though.
